description: Rewrite the Travel Tips page (traveltip.html + traveltip.css) onto the FEAT-001 foundation. Sections: best time to visit (with a semantic HTML <table> of months/regions), transport, etiquette, packing, food, safety, responsible tourism. Add a sticky table of contents on desktop (an <aside> of in-page anchors) that collapses gracefully on mobile. Fix the broken nav links (destinations.html → destination.html).
steps: Rewrite c:/Users/aadyagupta/Incredible-India/traveltip.html. Replace <head> with the canonical head block (title 'Travel Tips — Incredible India', unique meta description, fonts, favicon, styles.css + traveltip.css, inline `.js` script). Add the skip link, canonical header (aria-current="page" on Travel Tips), <main id="main">, canonical footer, <script src="site.js" defer></script>. Match the header/footer/logo byte-identically to the other pages.
Add one h1 (e.g. 'Travel Tips for India') and a short intro.

Build a two-column desktop layout: a sticky <aside class="toc"> on the left (list of anchor links to #best-time, #transport, #etiquette, #packing, #food, #safety, #responsible-tourism) and the content <article> on the right. The TOC must be position:sticky on desktop and collapse to a normal stacked block (or a simple list) on mobile — never overflow horizontally.

Add section 'Best time to visit' (id=best-time) containing a semantic <table> with a <caption>, <thead> (months), and rows for regions (e.g. North India, South India, Himalayas, Coastal) with a short note per cell (accurate; no invented prices). The table must scroll horizontally within its container on very narrow screens (wrap in a div with overflow-x:auto) so the page itself never scrolls horizontally.

Add sections (each with an id and an <h2>): transport (#transport), etiquette (#etiquette), packing (#packing), food (#food), safety (#safety), responsible tourism (#responsible-tourism) — each a short, accurate paragraph or list (no invented facts).

Rewrite c:/Users/aadyagupta/Incredible-India/traveltip.css for page-specific layout only (two-column sticky-TOC layout, table styling, section spacing). Reuse tokens from styles.css. Provide a mobile breakpoint that stacks the TOC above the content and makes the table horizontally scrollable.
Remove all Font Awesome markup and the broken nav links (destinations.html → destination.html already handled by using the canonical header).
acceptance_criteria: traveltip.html has the canonical head (unique title + meta description, fonts, favicon, styles.css + traveltip.css, inline .js script), skip link, canonical header (aria-current on Travel Tips), <main id="main">, canonical footer, site.js deferred — matching the other pages.
Seven sections exist with ids best-time, transport, etiquette, packing, food, safety, responsible-tourism.
A semantic <table> with <caption>, <thead>, and region rows exists under #best-time.
A sticky <aside class="toc"> of anchor links to all seven sections exists and is sticky on desktop, stacked on mobile.
No Font Awesome link; no broken nav links.
verification: `python -m http.server 8000`; open http://localhost:8000/traveltip.html — TOC links scroll to each section; the TOC is sticky while scrolling on desktop.
At 360px width the TOC stacks above content and the table scrolls within its box (page has no horizontal overflow).
No 404s for traveltip.css; no external resources.
